# dsh-phone
SMS, calls, live voicemail and Telegram in the DSH sidebar, with call audio through your own server.
Install from npm: `dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-phone`, or from GitHub: `dsh plugin
--profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-phone`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Screenshot from a demo DSH instance with sample data.
A phone in the DeepSeek Harness web GUI. It adds a **Phone** tab to the sidebar (dsh-better-sidebar)
DeepSeek Harness web GUI. It adds a **Phone** tab to the sidebar (dsh-better-sidebar) where you can:
- **Text**: SMS threads, send and receive, delivery status, MMS pictures, segment counter (GSM-7 / U

nicode).
- **Call**: place and answer calls in the browser, mute, keypad (DTMF), call log. **Call au
dio goes through your server by default** ("Via server": one encrypted wss socket to the DSH origin,
so it works on networks that block WebRTC and the browser talks to no third party); **Direct** (Web
RTC to Twilio through the Twilio Voice SDK) stays one click away. A **Test audio** button checks a n

etwork without placing a call.
- **Choose how calls reach you**, with one switch:
- **Live**: calls
ring this browser (and optionally a mobile, which must press 1 so its own voicemail cannot steal the

call). Unanswered calls go to voicemail.
- **Voicemail**: every call goes to voicemail. While the c
aller speaks you see a **live transcript** and can **Pick up** (hot answer), like iOS Live Voicemail

.
- **Do not disturb**: calls go to voicemail and nothing rings, chimes or notifies. Starred contact

s can still ring. Optional auto reply by SMS.
- **Voicemail**: greeting (spoken or an audio file), r
ecording stored on your server, final transcript by a **local Whisper** endpoint (good Greek, free)

or Mistral Voxtral, and the recording is deleted from the provider.
[该节后续省略]
## How it fits together
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- **phone-hookd** (`daemon/hookd.mjs`) is a small Node service that owns the database and talks to t

he provider. It has two listeners:
- a **public** one (`127.0.0.1:3098`, exposed only as `https://<h
ost>/phone-hook/`) for provider webhooks. Every request must carry a valid `X-Twilio-Signature`; any

thing else gets 403.
- a **private** unix socket (`~/.dsh/phone/hookd.sock`, mode 0600) used only by

the plugin.
It runs outside the web UI on purpose: calls still reach voicemail and texts still arri

ve while the UI restarts.
- **The plugin** (`lib/index.js`) runs inside dsh-web. It registers the se
ttings, the agent tools and `/dsh-phone/api/*`, where every request passes the same four gates as ds
h-mail / dsh-hpc (loopback peer, same-origin trust fence, short-lived capability token, harness sess

ion cookie) before it is forwarded to the socket. It also serves the Voice SDK locally (no CDN).
- *
*The browser half** (`src/client.jsx`, built to `lib/client.js`) starts one phone service per page:
live events (SSE), the Twilio Device, a WebAudio ringtone, browser notifications, and an overlay for
incoming calls, the active call, live voicemail and toasts, visible whichever tab is open.
## Install
Requirements: DSH web with `dsh-better-sidebar`, Node 22.5+ (for `node:sqlite`), a Twilio account wi
th a voice + SMS number, and a public HTTPS hostname your reverse proxy can route to a loopback port
h a voice + SMS number, and a public HTTPS hostname your reverse proxy can route to a loopback port.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Plugin only (the Phone tab and agent tools, when the daemon runs elsewhere): from npm `dsh plugin --
profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-phone`, or from GitHub `dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucagif
tzek/dsh-phone`. The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` lists it in the profile bund
/dsh-phone`. The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` lists it in the profile bundles.
Then open **Settings > Phone**: put the account SID and auth token in the fields or in a `KEY=value`
credentials file (`TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`; default `~/.config/twilio/credentials`
), add your number as a line (or pick it from "Numbers on the Twilio account"), set the public webho
ok base URL, **Save**, then **Apply to Twilio**. The checklist should go green, and the browser regi
sters so calls can ring.
## Call audio: Via server (default) or Direct
With **Via server** the browser captures the microphone (echo cancellation, noise suppression and au
to gain on), encodes G.711 mu-law in an AudioWorklet and sends 20 ms blocks over ONE wss socket to t
he DSH origin (`/dsh-phone/api/io`, about 70 kbit/s each way at the default 40 ms per message); far
audio plays through a small adaptive jitter buffer. No Twilio SDK, CDN, STUN or TURN is loaded. phon
e-hookd bridges the socket to the call:
- **SIP lines** (an Asterisk relay): hookd originates an AudioSocket channel over AMI into a generat
ed context that applies the line's destination policy and dials the provider. Audio between Asterisk

and hookd stays on 127.0.0.1. Twilio is not involved.
- **Twilio lines** and **every incoming call
you answer here**: a bidirectional Twilio Media Stream (`<Connect><Stream>`, mu-law 8 kHz) to `wss:/
/<host>/phone-hook/s`, accepted only with a valid `X-Twilio-Signature` over the wss URL and a one-ti
me ticket bound to the CallSid. Incoming calls ring the Phone tab through the event stream while the
caller hears ringback from the server; unanswered or declined calls go to voicemail as before, and

**Pick up** on a live voicemail works the same way.
- Per-call audio stats (route, packets and bytes
each way, jitter, first-audio time, end reason) are stored with the call log row, so a silent call

can be diagnosed from the server. Nothing is recorded beyond the voicemail you already have.
- Limit
s: `audio.maxCalls` (default 2) calls and `audio.maxTests` (2) tests at once; a dropped browser sock
et keeps the call for 15 s while the tab reconnects.
Choose the route per browser in the Phone tab (Keypad, "Call audio"), or set the default with `audio
he route per browser in the Phone tab (Keypad, "Call audio"), or set the default with `audio.route`.

## Security
See docs/SECURITY.md. In short: the only unauthenticated path is the signature-checked webhook prefi
x, served by a hardened daemon that never reaches the web UI; secrets are never returned by any read
endpoint; sending and calling from agents are opt-in and draft-first.
